chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Umar ibn Yazid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The delight of my eyes has been placed in salat (prayer), my pleasure in this world is women, and my two sweet-scented ones are Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn.'

key_terms.الصَّلَاة: Salat — the ritual prayer, the highest act of worship in Islam
key_terms.رَيْحَانَتَيَّ: My two sweet-scented ones — a term of endearment meaning 'my two fragrant flowers', applied to Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn
key_terms.قُرَّةُ عَيْنِي: Delight/coolness of my eye — a classical Arabic idiom for one's greatest joy and source of comfort
key_terms.لَذَّتِي: My pleasure/delight — the enjoyment found in worldly blessings

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about prayer, women, Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn?
ai.summary: This hadith reports the Prophet Muhammad's (SAWW) declaration of three things most beloved to him in this world: salat (ritual prayer), women (understood in the Islamic tradition as righteous wives and the blessing of companionship), and his two grandsons Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn (AS). The phrase 'qurrat al-'ayn' (coolness/delight of the eye) is a classical Arabic expression for the greatest joy and comfort of the soul. The mention of salat first reflects the Prophet's deep spiritual orientation — that his heart found its truest rest and nearness to God in prayer. The Prophet's use of the word 'rayhanatayn' (two sweet-scented flowers) for his grandsons Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn is a term of profound love and tenderness, expressing that they were a source of spiritual fragrance and blessing in his life.
